events.title: v0.1.0 The engine stands alone
events.detail: Split out of the code that rebuilt the DDWG introduction films: narration with a local speech model, soundtrack assembly, captions, picture staging and rendering, with a one-minute bilingual sample film.

events.title: v0.3.0 Concept contract and readings check
events.detail: A film declares what each concept means in its source and each edition's words for it; narration checks concepts and readings before any speech model loads.

events.title: v0.6.0 The picture gate
events.detail: check-picture runs the frame, sync and motion audits of the current composition and timeline and writes a gate record; without a passing record, nothing renders.

events.title: v0.8.0 Measured with the film's own fonts
events.detail: The headless audits measure text with the film's declared fonts; the gate record binds the stylesheet and each font by SHA-256.

events.title: v0.9.0 Named where it is spoken
events.detail: The gate refuses a mark that stands in speech for over 0.6 s before a name is legible, and speech of over 1 s with no legible name.

events.title: v0.10.0 The first production review
events.detail: The review command writes a film's first production review; before a render, preflight reports every stale or missing input at once.

events.title: v0.12.0 Every mark followed
events.detail: The motion audit follows each mark as a viewer sees it move and refuses halts, starts, races and pops; from this release it applies to every film.

events.title: v0.13.0 Uncaptioned pictures, four films
events.detail: Each edition renders a second picture without captions and proves it differs only by them; a delivery holds 25 members.

events.title: v0.14.0 Switches without a flash
events.detail: A version or captions switch in the player no longer shows the cover or a flat frame; the gate checks arcs that sweep a whole turn.

events.title: v0.17.0 Jumps and dash snaps
events.detail: The gate refuses marks that a stage cut moves whole, and strokes whose dashes snap within one frame.

events.title: v0.18.0 One author, no ringing
events.detail: The 1080p films average each 2×2 block between decode and encode, with a keyframe every 2 s; the verifier refuses films packaged earlier.

events.title: v0.19.0 Every frame compared
events.detail: compare-pictures compares every frame of an edition's two pictures and names each one-frame fault with the command that renders its picture again. Each film names its version, so a film packaged by an earlier release is refused.
